name: Ajax 1994/95
description: Ajax, Champions League winners in 1995, with a young core, positional play and wingers attacking down the flanks.

name: Arsenal 2005–11
description: Wenger's Arsenal, with short passes and combinations through the middle, a young core and no trophies in the Emirates era.

name: Atlético Madrid 2013/14
description: Simeone's Atlético, Spanish champions with a compact block, direct counter-attacks and intense zonal marking.

name: Barcelona 2008–12
description: Guardiola's Barcelona: long possession, short passing, high pressing and a core of academy players.

name: Brazil 1982
description: Telê Santana's squad at the 1982 World Cup in Spain: talent, technique and futebol-arte, with freedom for the stars.

name: Borussia Dortmund 2010–13
description: Klopp's Dortmund: counter-pressing, quick transitions and physical intensity, twice German champions.

name: Flamengo 1980
description: Coutinho's Flamengo: a technical side with the ball on the ground and freedom for the stars, 1980 Brazilian champions.

name: Fluminense 2023
description: Diniz's Fluminense: possession with short passing, position rotation and its own identity, Copa Libertadores champions in 2023.

name: Grêmio 2017
description: Renato's Grêmio: possession that goes forward with purpose, play through the middle and a focus on results, Libertadores champions in 2017.

name: Inter 2009/10
description: Mourinho's Inter: direct counter-attacks, a mid-to-low block, zonal marking and the treble.

name: Juventus 2014–19
description: Allegri's Juventus: pragmatic and adaptable, with a mid-to-low block, a focus on results and a tradition of winning titles.

name: Leeds United 2019/20
description: Bielsa's Leeds: very high pressing, man-marking, vertical attacks down the wings and a system that does not change.

name: Liverpool 2021/22
description: Klopp's Liverpool: a 4-3-3 with high pressing, relational rotations and full-backs providing width, almost winning everything.

name: Mamelodi Sundowns 2025
description: Cardoso's Mamelodi Sundowns: possession with combinations through the middle, zonal defence and technical players, with the plan adapted to each opponent.

name: Manchester City 2017/18
description: Guardiola's Manchester City: positional play, high pressing, a 4-3-3 with wingers and a technical, athletic squad, English champions with 100 points.

name: Manchester United 1995/96
description: Ferguson's Manchester United: a 4-4-2 with quick wingers, a young core and the coach's authority, focused on results.

name: Milan 1988–91
description: Sacchi's Milan: collective high pressing, pure zonal marking, a system above the stars and an identity imposed by the coach.

name: Milan 2006/07
description: Ancelotti's Milan: a midfield diamond with Pirlo as the pivot, freedom for Kaká and the stars, a mid block and a focus on results.

name: Netherlands 1974
description: Michels' Oranje: high pressing, total football with fluid roles, possession and a coach with strong authority.

name: Vasco 2026
description: Pedro Emanuel's Vasco: pressing and possession that goes forward quickly, attacks down the wings and a focus on results, with the plan adapted to each opponent.

name: Wolves 1949–60
description: Stan Cullis's Wolves: fast, direct, physical football built on intense preparation and discipline. League champions in 1954, 1958 and 1959.

name: Austria 1931–34 (Wunderteam)
description: Austria's Wunderteam: short passing and position swapping, with a withdrawn centre-forward.

name: Arsenal 1925–34
description: Herbert Chapman's Arsenal: a third back, the stopper, deep defending and counter-attacks. League champions in 1931 and 1933.

name: Hungary 1950–56 (Golden Team)
description: The Golden Team: a withdrawn centre-forward (Hidegkuti), mobile midfielders and first-time passing. Unbeaten from June 1950 to the 1954 World Cup final.

name: River Plate 1941–47 (La Máquina)
description: River Plate's La Máquina: forwards who swap positions, short passing and dribbling. The style that came to define Argentine football.

name: Queen's Park 1872–89
description: Queen's Park of Glasgow: combination play, short passing from player to player in a 2-2-6 shape. The root of the Scottish passing game.

name: Ajax 1971–73
description: Ajax under Ștefan Kovács, European champions in 1972 and 1973: total football, with high pressing, possession and constant position swaps.

name: Argentina 1978
description: Menotti's Argentina, world champions at home: an attacking side with possession and high pressing, using wide wingers.

name: Argentina 1986
description: Bilardo's Argentina, world champions in Mexico: a 3-5-2 with man-marking, counter-attacks and Maradona as the star.

name: Atlético Nacional 1989
description: Maturana's Atlético Nacional, 1989 Libertadores winners: possession with short passing, zonal marking and freedom for the players.

name: Barcelona 1990–94
description: Cruyff's Dream Team, four-time Spanish champions and 1992 European champions: possession, positional play and attacks using the wingers.

name: Bayern 1973–76
description: Three-time European champions Bayern: a veteran, results-first side with man-marking and Beckenbauer as an attacking sweeper.

name: Boca Juniors 2000–01
description: Bianchi's Boca, Libertadores winners in 2000 and 2001 and Intercontinental Cup winners in 2000: counter-attacks, man-marking and an experienced squad.

name: Brazil 1970
description: The three-time world champions in Mexico under Zagallo: talent and technique, possession, wing play and great freedom for the stars.

name: Chile 2015–16
description: Sampaoli's Chile, 2015 Copa América winners: high pressing, possession and attacks down the flanks.

name: Colombia 1990–94
description: Maturana's Colombia: short passing, zonal marking and a creative central midfielder, in a possession side with its own identity.

name: Dynamo Kyiv 1974–75
description: Lobanovskyi's Dynamo Kyiv, Cup Winners' Cup and Super Cup winners in 1975: pressing, system above names and the coach's authority.

name: Dynamo Kyiv 1985–86
description: Lobanovskyi's Dynamo Kyiv, 1986 Cup Winners' Cup winners: high pressing, counter-attacks and system discipline.

name: Estudiantes 1967–70
description: Zubeldía's Estudiantes, three-time Libertadores winners (1968–70): a defensive side with man-marking, set pieces and discipline.

name: Flamengo 2019
description: Jorge Jesus's Flamengo, 2019 Libertadores and Brazilian champions: high pressing, vertical play and its own identity.

name: Independiente 1972–75
description: Four-time Libertadores winners Independiente: counter-attacks, an offside line and an experienced defence.

name: Inter 1963–65
description: Herrera's Inter, European champions in 1964 and 1965: catenaccio, man-marking, counter-attacks and the coach's authority.

name: Bayer Leverkusen 2023/24
description: Xabi Alonso's Leverkusen, unbeaten German champions: positional play, progression through the middle and a system above its stars.

name: Liverpool 1976–84
description: Paisley and Fagan's Liverpool, European champions in 1977, 1978, 1981 and 1984: a 4-4-2 of patient possession and counter-attacks, with zonal marking.

name: Nottingham Forest 1978–80
description: Clough's Nottingham Forest, English champions in 1978 and European champions in 1979 and 1980: counter-attacks, passing on the ground and the coach's authority.

name: Palmeiras 2020–21
description: Abel Ferreira's Palmeiras, Libertadores winners in 2020 and 2021: pragmatic, adapting to the opponent, with counter-attacks and a mid or low block.

name: Peñarol 1960–66
description: Peñarol, Libertadores winners in 1960, 1961 and 1966: defending and counter-attacking, with direct play and a focus on results.

name: Real Madrid 1955–60
description: Five-time European champions Real Madrid: a team of stars like Di Stéfano and Puskás, with direct play and roving attacks down the flanks.

name: River Plate 2014–19
description: Gallardo's River, Libertadores winners in 2015 and 2018: possession, high pressing and its own identity.

name: Santos 1962–63
description: Pelé's Santos, two-time Libertadores and world club champions: an attacking, adaptable side with talent and wing play.

name: São Paulo 1992–93
description: Telê Santana's São Paulo, two-time Libertadores and world club champions: possession, spectacle football and the coach's authority.

name: Spain 2008–12
description: Spain, winners of Euro 2008, the 2010 World Cup and Euro 2012: intense possession, play through the middle and technique.

name: Uruguay 1950
description: Uruguay, world champions after the Maracanazo: counter-attacks, man-marking and the captain as the group's leader.
